title: Diagnosing Drain Ventilation Failures
description: When fixtures drain slowly or emit unpleasant sewer gases despite a clean trap, the issue often lies hidden in the drain ventilation system. Vent stacks allow air to enter the plumbing network, equalizing pressure so wastewater can flow freely. Without adequate air intake, rushing water creates a vacuum effect, siphoning water out of fixture traps or causing sluggish, gurgling drains. Professional troubleshooting requires inspecting the roof termination point for obstructions like leaves, nests, or ice buildup. Understanding how atmospheric pressure interacts with your drainage network is essential for accurate diagnostics and lasting repairs.
